paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when you're under pressure, run TO God, not around Him. David opens with "O LORD my God, I take refuge in You…" (Psalm 7:1), and he says it while people are chasing him. Then he lays his whole case before the LORD, even saying "if injustice is on my hands…" (Psalm 7:3). I think that is brave, because he asks God to look at the real him.

Why can he do that? Because God is not like a friend who sends a thumbs-up while fuming inside. David calls Him a "righteous God who searches hearts and minds" (Psalm 7:9), and says "God is a righteous judge…" (Psalm 7:11). That means the baker can trust Him with the unfair stuff, the stuff nobody else sees, and nobody gets away with anything. David also says that if one does not repent, God will sharpen His sword (Psalm 7:12), so God's justice is real and it is serious.

And look where David lands. The wicked man "has fallen into a pit of his own making" (Psalm 7:15), while David says "My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart" (Psalm 7:10). So the baker doesn't have to get even, because God is the one who judges. That's why David ends with "I will thank the LORD for His righteousness and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High" (Psalm 7:17). Take refuge in Him, be honest with Him, and let your thank-you songs get LOUD, friend.
